title: Wet Cat Rug
text: Wet Cat Rug. Close your eyes. No, wait, open them, I need you to keep reading or this won't work. So, keep your eyes open, but kind of act like they should be closed. Better. Now, imagine yourself stepping out of the shower. It smells amazing. (You just went to LUSH, so this was quite possibly a holy experience here.) You feel great. You grab your towel. It is perfectly dried, still smells a little like your fabric softener but is that perfect towel feel. Everything is perfect. Then you step on a wet cat! Wait. What? You look down, hoping your cat isn't really under your feet. Nope. Just this rug. This cat fur rug. That looked so super chic when you placed it in front of the shower. It looked great with my coral honeycomb pattern shower curtain. A perfect postmodern mesh. But wet cat feel just ruined the shower experience. You try to figure out how to get off the wet cat rug. You figure you'll just finish drying off, since it is a bathroom rug and will certainly at least absorb the water rolling off your body. You'd be wrong, again. Wet cat is surprisingly unabsorbent. So after your shower, you have to dry the floor, since the wet cat proved worthless at his job. But at least he looks snazzy. No? No. He looks like a wet cat laying in front of your shower. A mangled wet dumpster cat. This is bad. Maybe when it dries it will be better? A little. But not the chic look you had before. Now your cat is dry, but has some odd cowlicks he didn't have before. Who thought faux fur would be a good idea in a bathroom? And why did I think it'd be a good idea? Did no one stop and say, "Hey, this might feel awful when wet and look like a wet cat?" I mean, I didn't. But I don't get paid to make cat rugs.
